formal_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (j u t : ℕ), PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C → j < C.gates.length → C.gates[j]? = some { op := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or, inputs := [u, t] } → t < n + j → (∀ x : Fin n → Bool, (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD t false = true → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.circuitFun n C x = true) → ∀ (S : List ℕ) (k : ℕ), PEqualNP.ReadK.readsAtMost C n S k = true → PEqualNP.ReadK.readsAtMost { gates := C.gates.set j { op := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or, inputs := [u] } ++ [{ op := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or, inputs := [C.output, t] }], output := n + C.gates.length } n S k = true
plain_statement: C is a circuit of AND and OR gates, each listing at most two wires (a wire not yet made reads false, with no proof tree). Gate j is the OR of wires u and t, t an earlier wire, and wherever t is true the output is true. The lifted circuit replaces gate j by an OR reading u alone and appends, as its output, an OR of the old output and t. For every list S of input indices and every k: if some proof tree of the old output (one wire per OR, all wires per AND, leaves in S) has each member of S as a leaf at most k times, so does some proof tree of the lifted output.
title: Implicant lift never raises read: if an AND/OR fan-in-two circuit is read-k on a variable list, so is its lifted circuit
